newsitem.title: CHINA: China M2 grows 27.5 pct in Jan-Aug - central bank.
newsitem.headline: China M2 grows 27.5 pct in Jan-Aug - central bank.

text.p: China's broad M2 money supply rose by 27.5 percent in January to August compared with the year-ago period, the China Securities on Friday quoted the People's Bank of China, the central bank, as saying.
China's M1, or currency in circulation plus current deposits, rose by 15.1 percent in the first eight months compared with the year-ago period, the bank said.
It said the growth of broad M2 was drawing closer to a government target of 25 percent.
Central bank governor Dai Xianglong said earlier this month that China's broad M2 money supply was expected to rise by 23 percent a year through the year 2000.
M1 was expected to rise by 18 percent a year through 2000, Dai said.
In July, China's M2 rose by 27 percent year-on-year while M1 rose by 15 percent.
China has set a target for M2 growth of 25 percent for all of 1996 and a target of 18 percent for M1.
